title: Adaptive Methods Are Preferable in High Privacy Settings: An SDE Perspective
claim: Empirical loss scales as 1/ε² for the non-adaptive method and 1/ε for adaptive ones, matching theory across tasks.
layout: 3 line-plot panels in a row, shared legend style, log-like decay curves
description: Three side-by-side line plots titled Quadratic, IMDB and StackOverflow. Each plots expected loss E[f(X_T)] on the y-axis against privacy budget epsilon on the x-axis, with grid lines and a legend in the upper right. Colored lines with markers show DP-SGD (purple stars), DP-SignSGD (green circles) and DP-Adam (orange triangles), with shaded error bands. The left panel adds dashed theoretical-bound curves in blue and yellow that sit on top of the empirical DP-SGD and DP-SignSGD curves. The center and right panels add black dash-dotted O(ε^-2) and blue dashed O(ε^-1) reference curves. The DP-SGD curve rises steeply at small epsilon, while DP-SignSGD and DP-Adam stay low and flat. The eye goes first to the steep purple curve at low epsilon.
caption: Empirical validation of the privacy-utility trade-off predicted by Thm. [ref] and Thm. [ref], comparing \algname{DP-SGD}, \algname{DP-SignSGD}, and \algname{DP-Adam}: Our focus is on verifying the functional dependence of the asymptotic loss levels in terms of $\varepsilon$. Left: On a quadratic convex function $f(x)=\tfrac{1}{2}x^\top Hx$, the observed empirical loss values perfectly match the theoretical predictions (Eq. [ref], Eq. [ref]). Center and Right: Logistic regressions on the IMDB dataset (center) and the StackOverflow dataset (right), confirm the same pattern: the utility of \algname{DP-SGD} scales as $\tfrac{1}{\varepsilon^2}$, while the utility of \algname{DP-SignSGD} scales linearly as $\tfrac{1}{\varepsilon}$. Across all settings, we observe that the insights obtained for \algname{DP-SignSGD} extend to \algname{DP-Adam} as well as to the test loss (see Figure [ref]). For experimental details see Appendix [ref].
abstract: Differential Privacy (DP) is becoming central to large-scale training as privacy regulations tighten. We revisit how DP noise interacts with adaptivity in optimization through the lens of stochastic differential equations, providing the first SDE-based analysis of private optimizers. Focusing on DP-SGD and DP-SignSGD under per-example clipping, we show a sharp contrast under fixed hyperparameters: DP-SGD converges at a Privacy-Utility Trade-Off of $\mathcal{O}(1/\varepsilon^2)$ with speed independent of $\varepsilon$, while DP-SignSGD converges at a speed linear in $\varepsilon$ with an $\mathcal{O}(1/\varepsilon)$ trade-off, dominating in high-privacy or large batch noise regimes. By contrast, under optimal learning rates, both methods achieve comparable theoretical asymptotic performance; however, the optimal learning rate of DP-SGD scales linearly with $\varepsilon$, while that of DP-SignSGD is essentially $\varepsilon$-independent. This makes adaptive methods far more practical, as their hyperparameters transfer across privacy levels with little or no re-tuning. Empirical results confirm our theory across training and test metrics, and empirically extend from DP-SignSGD to DP-Adam.
